title: Noor and the Prom
premise: Vesper Vane has spent seventeen years hiding behind her locker door and her perfect grades, letting her bread do the talking — loaves that taste like grief, rolls that taste like first crushes. When the senior class college essay prompt asks 'Who are you when no one is watching?' her honest answer leaks online, and suddenly everyone at Halcyon High can taste who she really is. As prom approaches, Vesper falls for Noor Haddad, the student body president whose polished image depends on keeping Vesper quiet, forcing both girls to choose between the selves they perform and the ones they've baked into being. In the end, Vesper serves truth to the whole school at prom itself, loses the scholarship she was hiding for, and gains something rarer: a self she doesn't have to swallow.
about_author: Beatrix Pemberton is a former bakery counter girl from coastal Maine who writes stories about teenagers who feel too much and say too little. She believes every kitchen is a confessional and every recipe an unfinished letter.

chapters.title: The Locker Rule
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. We meet Vesper mid-ritual: head down, grades up, locker shut, delivering anonymous 'feeling bread' to classmates who never know it's hers. A grief loaf for a grieving teacher nearly exposes her. Emotional beat: the comfort and suffocation of invisibility.

chapters.title: Yeast and Silence
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At her family's bakery, Vesper's father warns her that bread tells truths people aren't ready to eat. She bakes a batch of 'nothing' bread — flavorless, safe — and hates how good she's gotten at it. Beat: establishing the family stakes and her self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. English class receives the college essay prompt: 'Who are you when no one is watching?' The room goes quiet in a way Vesper recognizes from her own kitchen. That night she writes one honest paragraph and immediately regrets it. Beat: the inciting crack in her armor.

chapters.title: Noor Haddad, Perfect
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Noor. Student body president Noor Haddad rehearses her scholarship speech like a recipe she must not alter. She notices Vesper's essay draft left in the shared printer tray and reads one line before stopping herself. Beat: two performers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What Leaks
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The essay — submitted to a supposedly private portal — appears on the school gossip account, verbatim. By lunch, half the cafeteria has read that Vesper bakes feelings into bread and feels 'like a loaf nobody ordered.' Beat: exposure, humiliation, the labels arriving.

chapters.title: Sourdough Fame
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Overnight, Vesper becomes a curiosity: kids beg her for custom loaves, teachers request 'confidence croissants,' and the principal wants a word about 'appropriate use of school portals.' Vesper discovers attention is just another kind of hiding. Beat: power arrives uninvited.

chapters.title: Rye for the President
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor orders a loaf anonymously — then chickens out and picks it up in person. The bread tastes like exhaustion and ambition gone stale. She realizes Vesper can taste what no one says aloud, which makes her dangerous. Beat: attraction braided with fear.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Noor recruits Vesper to bake for prom, officially as community service, unofficially to keep her close and controlled. Vesper agrees because the prom gig comes with a scholarship recommendation Noor controls. Beat: love and leverage entangled from the start.

chapters.title: Test Kitchen
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Late-night baking sessions in the closed bakery. Noor talks while kneading — about her mother's expectations, the scholarship she needs more than she admits. Vesper bakes her something honest; Noor eats it and cries and pretends she didn't. Beat: intimacy through flour.

chapters.title: The Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A rival spreads a rumor that Noor is only using Vesper for the prom press. Cornered at an assembly, Noor publicly distances herself from Vesper to protect her image. Vesper watches from the crowd, holding a basket of warm rolls no one takes. Beat: first betrayal, duty over love.

chapters.title: Stale
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper stops baking feeling-bread entirely; everything she makes turns out flat and bitter. Her father recognizes the taste of heartbreak and finally tells her his own story of a dream he buried to survive. Beat: the price of survival made visible across generations.

chapters.title: The Scholarship File
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor discovers the scholarship committee plans to give Vesper's slot to a donor's nephew — and that her own recommendation could override it, if she spends political capital she's been hoarding for years. Beat: Noor faces what her power is actually for.

chapters.title: Bread and Circuses
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The school exploits Vesper's gift: administrators want 'morale muffins' after budget cuts gut the arts program. Vesper realizes they don't want her honesty — they want her sweetness as anesthesia. Beat: corruption of a gift into a tool.

chapters.title: What Noor Won't Say
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Vesper bakes a confrontation loaf and leaves it in Noor's locker: it tastes exactly like the thing Noor refuses to say. Noor tracks Vesper down in the empty bakery, and they almost kiss before the alarm goes off — literally and otherwise. Beat: desire at full heat, interrupted.

chapters.title: The Essay Prompt, Again
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper rewrites her college essay — this time about Noor, about choosing visibility, about bread as confession. Her counselor warns that admissions officers want polish, not raw dough. Vesper submits it anyway. Beat: committing to truth before knowing the cost.

chapters.title: Leaked Twice
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The new essay leaks too — but this time Vesper suspects Noor's rival did it to destroy them both. The school turns on Vesper as a 'drama queen,' and the scholarship committee flags her file. Beat: rising dread; the system closing in.

chapters.title: Noor's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor confronts her rival and her own complicity, then does the unthinkable: she spends every ounce of her accumulated capital demanding the committee reinstate Vesper, on record, publicly. It costs her the presidency and her mother's approval. Beat: love against duty, duty losing.

chapters.title: Flour Fight
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The night before prom, Noor shows up at the bakery covered in rain and apology. They fight, laugh, and finally kiss in a cloud of flour. Together they plan something for tomorrow that the school won't see coming. Beat: the emotional climax's calm before the storm.

chapters.title: Prom, Unlabeled
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At prom, instead of the requested dessert table, Vesper serves one loaf per guest — each tasting of that person's truest unsaid thing. The gym dissolves into tears, laughter, and confessions. The principal tries to shut it down; the students refuse. Beat: public climax, truth served warm.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Fallout: the scholarship is revoked for 'conduct unbecoming,' and Vesper's college acceptance wobbles. But classmates testify, the story spreads beyond the school, and an independent baking fellowship reaches out. Beat: loss and unexpected grace arriving together.

chapters.title: Crumb by Crumb
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor rebuilds without her title — smaller, truer, running an honest student fund with money she raised by telling her own story. She and Vesper negotiate what they are when neither is performing. Beat: love re-founded on choice rather than crisis.

chapters.title: Who I Am When Everyone Is Watching
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue-style. Graduation day. Vesper answers the essay prompt aloud in her valedictory-adjacent moment: she is the girl who stopped swallowing herself. She hands Noor a small loaf that tastes like beginning. Final beat: survival, paid for, worth it.
